newsitem.title: UK: ICI says pound may dent profit 150 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: ICI says pound may dent profit 150 mln stg.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc said on Thursday that if the pound continued at current levels it would reduce full-year pre-tax profits by around 150 million stg.

"We estimate that the strength of the pound has cost us 90 million pounds so far this year, and if it stays at these levels the result is likely to be about 150 million pounds over the full year," chief financial officer Alan Spall told a news conference after interim results.
Spall said that of the 90 million stg hit in the first half, two-thirds stemmed from ICI's transaction exposure to the pound's strength as opposed to translation exposure.
But Spall also said ICI's new portfolio, which consists of fewer bulk chemical activities, which were mainly based in the UK, had made the company less vulnerable to the pound.

Chief executive Charles Miller Smith added: "The shift of ICI up the value chain and the shift away from exporting businesses means ICI will have more translation rather than transaction exposure. That is clearly advantageous."
